messages:
kevin (PM): ACME asked to move tenant-level backup & restore into MVP or else they can't pilot. quick gut check: ship MVP with a narrow restore path or push to v1?

anya (eng): Full backup/restore is a big migration risk. We could provide a scoped restore: daily snapshots + on-demand restore for pilot tenants only. That
uts the scope.

maria (cs): ACME specifically needs the ability to restore a tenant to a point-in-time within the last 24h. They accept pilot-only and a documented window.

tom (sre): Scoped restore (24h PIT, S3-stored snapshots, tenant isolation) is doable. Estimate ~1 sprint ops+eng with a gated feature flag and runbook. Need retention policy and test harness.

kevin (PM): Proposal: "MVP: 24h PIT restore (pilot)" behind feature flag `tenant_pit_restore`. Pilot limited to ACME + two internal tenants. Acceptance criteria: successful restore in staging, tenant isolation tests, restore <30m for 90% of restores.

legal-bot: Reminder: restore capability may expose customer data copies; require data processing addendum for pilot. Legal review needed.

anya (eng): Implementation notes: incremental snapshot every 6h + on-demand restore job. Defer full DB-level migration tools to v1. We'll add smoke tests for config and data integrity.

maria (cs): I'll draft pilot onboarding steps and customer-facing limitations. ACME will want a rollback SLA if restore breaks.

kevin (PM): Action items:
- kevin: add milestone to tracker + acceptance criteria (today)
- anya: spike impl plan + perf estimates (due Tue)
- tom: infra runbook + retention config (due Tue)
- maria: pilot comms + limitations doc (due Wed)
- legal-bot: start intake for DPA addendum

kevin (PM): We'll mark this as a constrained MVP change; if pilot fails or legal objects, revert the flag and schedule full restore capability for v1. 15m sync tomorrow to lock owners.

anya (eng): one developer note: restores touch multiple services (cache, search, embeddings store). We'll list those dependencies in the spike.

maria (cs): ACME said pilot-only is acceptable as long as timeline is firm. I'll confirm tonight.

kevin (PM): thanks team :thumbsup:
